terra.problem: The joke about the exclamation point makes the way Scripture is written the punchline.
The jar-lid joke compares Papa's mistake to the baker's answer, making the choice question the subject of the joke.
Doing something without pity is not the opposite of doing it with regret.
“Wrong verse” uses “wrong” about the baker's answer.
The explanation reduces what the verse says about Israel and the Daughter of Judah to a statement about one city.
The verse says the Lord despised the priest; it does not say whether the priest was spared from harm.
“Both” distinguishes the king and priest in the final clause, but it does not carry the whole verse, which also describes other losses.
Finding no vision from the LORD does not establish that the prophets had nothing to pass along or that the city was quiet.
The verse says the prophets found no vision from the LORD, not that nothing at all was given to them or that they had nothing to pass along.
“The next stop” refers to the lesson's structure, which Papa does not discuss.
Papa comments on how he is telling the passage when he says he is not going to joke about it.
“Same word twice, so I think he means it” makes the repetition in Scripture the joke.
The verse does not say that the prophets' failure to expose guilt is what made their visions empty.
The final sentence says the passersby are grieving in one verse and scorning in the other. The grieving young women and the scorning passersby are different people.
The enemies say they waited for the day; the passage does not say they expected it.
